speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and what it looks like today?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Leishmaniasis (cutaneous).

I have noted your history of diabetes, Crohn's disease, and the ant bite; could you please describe the current size, shape, and any signs of spreading or bone exposure at the ulcer site?
